Y8_W06.big_idea: Linked measurements (a correlation) let a scatter graph and line of best fit estimate one from the other; people vary, so give a range.
goals: I can measure foot length and height, plot a scatter graph and draw a line of best fit.
I can estimate the footprint owner's height as a range from my graph and name suspects who fit.

flow.what: New case leader intro; 3 Week 5 recap questions from the evidence log; Parking Board; goals
True-size footprint by a metre stick: can it tell height? Vote short, medium or tall
Scatter graph, correlation, line of best fit; read off a range; model measuring safely, kindly
Measure in pairs, class data table, plot scatter graph, line of best fit, read off at 24 cm
Which suspects fit the range? Pair talk; evidence log row 6, tracker; exit ticket with vote

Y8_W06.practical: Pairs measure foot length (shoes off, 0.5 cm) and height (1 cm), plot a scatter graph and read off at 24 cm.
Y8_W06.assessment: Scatter graph and estimate (rubric strand 4); evidence log row 6, tracker, W6 confidence; exit ticket with Week 7 vote

prep_lines.text: Meet current teacher: handover, tracker, freezer decision, Weeks 6, 7 kit
Read Case Bible Sections 4 to 6 (suspects' heights and foot lengths)
Send print job (rebuilt designs): worksheets, data cards, signs, kit card
Print footprint at 100% (not fit to page): 6 per class plus 1; check 24 cm
Laminate the 7 sample data cards in A5 pouches (optional)
Borrow 6 hardbacks; collect rulers, metre sticks, trays; sharpen 24 pencils
Find the Week 5 Ideas Parking Board or its photo for the Do Now
Set up 2 or 3 height stations (chart or metre stick, sign); check the scale
Check the slide 9 data table can be typed into while projected

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Decide: class's own data or sample data (sample if class small)

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Set out group trays, case files, role and frame cards; Hook kit at front
Clean-up: shoes on, kit counted, data cards collected, footprints filed
Read exit tickets: record Week 7 option choices, give each group one option
Last class: return kit and books, store data cards; leave charts if needed

print_items: Worksheet x24 (2 sheets each, double-sided)
Scene footprint x6 per class, A4 at 100%, check 24 cm (1 per group)
Sample class data card x6, A5, laminated if possible (1 per group)
Height station sign x3, A4 (1 per station)
Teacher copies: kit card (A5), sample data card, Hook footprint
get_items: Rulers, 30 cm x12 (2 per group)
Metre sticks or tape measures x7 (6 groups, 1 Hook)
Hardback books x6 (borrow from library or staff room)
Paper height charts, 130 to 190 cm x3 (buy ready-made)
Masking tape x1 roll
Up to 3 metre sticks for upright stations (optional)
Laminating pouches, A5 x7 (optional)
Make: height stations x3 (chart, masking tape, sign)
reuse_items: Role card and frame card sets x6 each
hazards: Shoes off, socks on: shoes under desks, back on before anyone leaves their seat
No standing on chairs or tables; never swing metre sticks; retract tapes slowly
Measuring is voluntary: numbers not names, no comments on size; sample data allowed
watch_out: Measuring slow or under 16 measured: switch all to the sample data card; never mix data on one graph.
Joining dots, starting at zero or one number: ask 'As many crosses above as below?' Insist on a range.
Y8_W06.language_note: Frame: 'The person was probably between ___ cm and ___ cm tall.' Say 'height', not 'high'. Chinese answers count.
Y8_W06.next_week: Exit tickets: give each group one option (Soil, Paper, Ink 2, Powder 2), sets Week 8 kit; collect Week 7 soil

Y8_W07.big_idea: A good forensic test has a clear question, tests the scene sample exactly like the references, changes one thing and is planned to be safe.
goals: I can write a testable question and name what we change, observe or measure, and keep the same.
I can plan a safe method with reference samples, repeats, a risk table and a results table.

flow.what: Three recap questions on whiteboards or in the logbook; Today slide with goals and key words
Show sealed Evidence 6 and 7 bags; hand out option cards; Reporters read the question aloud
Six planning steps modelled with the Week 4 powder test; one worked risk-table row (vinegar)
Groups plan on the plan sheet; checkpoints at minutes 6 and 12; results table and kit request
Pick the fairer soil method; plan swap (skip if short); exit ticket; collect sheets at the door

Y8_W07.practical: No practical: groups plan their Week 8 test (Soil, Paper, Ink 2 or Powder 2) and only look at sealed bags.
Y8_W07.assessment: Plan sheet (rubric strands 1 and 2) signed off at checkpoints 1 and 2; exit ticket; kit requests; evidence log row 7.

prep_lines.text: Book printing: plan sheets x24 (48 sheets), kit card, Week 8 kit lists
Allocate options, print 10 option cards, make Evidence 6 and 7 bags
Evidence 3 bags: unopened Week 4 bag, or about 3 tsp baking soda each
Note ink strips N: Week 3 spares or new with pen B, in clear sleeves
Laminate the 10 option cards (optional)
Collect reference soils A to D and papers P1 to P4 (optional)

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Set out group kits, class box items; Evidence 6 and 7 on teacher desk
Clean-up: bags and N strips to teacher, keep option cards, wipe boards
Read plan sheets: check risk tables, one comment each, read exit tickets
Turn the six kit requests into Week 8 tray lists

print_items: Plan sheet x24 (4 A4 pages: 2 sheets each, double-sided)
Option cards x10 (1 sheet each, single-sided: 6 group, 4 spare)
Teacher copies: kit card (A5), Week 8 kit lists by option (4 A5)
get_items: Sealed evidence bags, up to 2 each: Evidence 6, 7, 3
Note ink strips N x2 (Week 3 spares first)
Small zip bags x6
Sticky labels x6
Clear plastic sleeves x2
Lab paper towel sheets x2 (from the lab's own roll)
Baking soda 6 tsp, if no sealed Week 4 bag (optional)
Coffee-filter strips 2 cm x 10 cm x2 (optional)
Mini whiteboards x24 (optional)
Dry-wipe pens x24 (optional)
Laminating pouches A4 x10 (optional)
Reference soils A to D, papers P1 to P4 (optional)
reuse_items: Role card sets x6 (with buddy card)
Pen B, for new N strips (optional)
hazards: No practical work: evidence bags stay sealed and go back to the teacher.
Do not open, smell or taste any sample.
Teacher checks every group's risk table before any Week 8 practical.
watch_out: Groups change two things, list kit instead of a method, or skip repeats: insist on the 'We change' frame.
Evidence 6 must come from flowerbed A; Evidence 7 from the lab's own roll, arrow marked before crumpling.
Y8_W07.language_note: Frames: 'We change / observe / keep ___'. Hazard is the thing, risk the chance. Band 1: language buddy, Core b) first.
Y8_W07.next_week: Week 8 lab day: commented plan sheets back in the Do Now; keep option cards and bags; trays from kit requests.

Y8_W08.big_idea: Doing a planned test carefully, repeating it and recording every result straight away (surprises too) makes a result trustworthy evidence.
goals: I can carry out our plan safely, repeat the test and record results with units in a table.
I can say what our result matches, how reliable it is and what it does or does not show.

flow.what: Safety Officer reads kit card aloud; group checks tray against kit request; roles confirmed.
Jury's three questions: repeated? references tested the same way? contaminated?
Safety slide, goggles on; record straight away, units, one line through, circle anomalies.
Pairs run parallel repeats, scene sample last; record on sheet; photos 18 to 21; tidy from 21.
Worksheet; Reporter round, 20 seconds per group; evidence log row 8; exit ticket at the door.

Y8_W08.practical: Groups run their Week 7 plan (Soil, Paper, Ink 2 or Powder 2) as two pairs doing parallel repeats.
Y8_W08.assessment: Recording sheet and worksheet (strand 3, part of strand 4) into case files; evidence log row 8; exit ticket; photos.

prep_lines.text: Print job 1: worksheets (48 sheets), run sheet A4 and A3, backup cards
Buy or request consumables; ask canteen for napkins; check filters, tape
Collect, rinse 20 identical 300 ml plastic screw-lid bottles per Soil class
Once options are allocated, print recording sheets x10 and kit cards x10
Write a tray list per group from Week 7 plans; note each class's split
Gather prep-room kit, check pens A to D; bag soils A to D and Evidence 6
Soil: if very wet, dry it on newspaper overnight (optional)
Ink 2 pen pre-test (salt water, vinegar); keep dried strips as answer key
Powder 2 pots (allergy check first); Ink 2 strips and vinegar; backup cards
Paper: make Evidence 7, cut and label P1 to P4, colour the water
Paper: pre-cut strips if the class is slow with scissors (optional)

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Fill Soil pots, set out bottles and one checked tray per group
Wash, restock trays; stick in Ink 2 strips; empty soil bottles after Week 9
Save photos, board notes; read and file work; photograph soil bottles again

print_items: Worksheet x24 (3 pages on 2 sheets: pages 1 and 2 double-sided)
Recording sheets x10 (1 sheet, double-sided; 12 if before allocation)
Kit cards x10 (A5, or 2 per A4 sheet; 4 are for the teacher's file)
Run sheet A3 enlargement x1 (wall)
Teacher copies: run sheet A4, backup cards (1 sheet, cut into 4)

Labels x39, markers x2, A4 paper x4, soil bags x5
Filter strips 2 cm by 10 cm x50, plus spares
Small plastic cups x44; stirring sticks x22
Timers x5, scissors x4, bucket x1, extra trays x2
Teaspoons x3, tablespoons x10, flat sticks x2
Water jugs x4; measuring jugs or cylinders x4
Small bottles for Ink 2 vinegar x2 (about 60 ml each)
Gloves, cloths, paper towels; camera or tablet x1
White vinegar 180 ml, plus a little for the pre-test
Baking soda 12, salt 7, cornflour 2, flour 2 level tsp
Tissues x2, canteen napkins x2, food colouring 6 drops
Make: soils A to D; Evidence 3, 6 and 7 (x2 each)
Make: P1 to P4 x2, Powder 2 sets x2, N strips x14
Make: pre-test strips x6, coloured water 600 ml
Optional: iodine dropper bottles x2, newspaper
reuse_items: Week 7 plan sheets and option cards
Goggles x20, magnifiers x5, rulers x7
Trays x6, tiles x4, droppers x2, tape x4
Pots x23, spoons x10, black card x2
Pens A to D x2 sets; kitchen roll
hazards: Goggles for vinegar, iodine, shaking soil bottles; lids tight; plastic bottles only
Never taste; Powder 2 allergy check (wheat, corn): an allergic student is Recorder
Soil: cover cuts or wear gloves, wash hands, never down the sink; iodine by dropper
watch_out: Check every tray before students arrive: with 24 Do minutes, a missing item costs a group its repeat.
No rubbing out: one line through, circle anomalies. A match is weak or supporting evidence, never proof.
Y8_W08.language_note: Frame: 'The scene sample matches ___ because ___ .' Traps: repeat vs replace, reliable vs accurate. Chinese welcome.
Y8_W08.next_week: Week 9: soil bottles stay labelled on the windowsill (look, do not open); keep photos, board notes, strips.

Y8_W09.big_idea: No single clue proves who took the notebook: rank evidence by how many suspects it fits, set aside contaminated evidence with a checked reason.
goals: I can rank evidence as strong, supporting or weak, and explain why the puddle is set aside.
I can write a CER conclusion with a confidence level and explain how tunnel vision misleads.

flow.what: Count each suspect's ticks in the suspect tracker: nobody matches everything. Slides 2 to 3.
Week 5 Ideas Parking Board photo: students find their note; today we check them. Slide 4.
Strong fits one suspect, supporting two, weak three or four; a combination can be strong.
Build A3 board (7 min); cleaning log card, set Evidence 4 aside (4 min); own CER (7 min).
Cartoon and parking board sort (3); roles and frames (4); self-assessment (4); exit ticket (1).

Y8_W09.practical: No practical: groups build an A3 evidence board from evidence cards, then set aside the contaminated puddle.
Y8_W09.assessment: CER and photographed board: rubric strands 4 and 5, into the case file. Collect self-assessment slips and exit tickets.

prep_lines.text: Book the Week 9 print job with reprographics (all classes)
Read Case Bible Section 9 and the answer key (all classes)
Collect and count the printed worksheets, boards, frames and slips
Check stock; print and cut 6 card packs; cut 24 slips and 6 badges
Print 6 cleaning log cards, seal in envelope; decide roles, number badges
Slide 4 photo; photograph soil bottles; gather Week 8 photos, notes
Optional: print the concept cartoon and put it up
Optional, if time is short: pre-fill 'Matches' lines on the 6 card packs

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Set out case files and resources; teacher desk in hand-out order
Photograph every evidence board
Clean-up: work into case files; collect them, slips, tickets; badges to box
Empty soil bottles on a flowerbed or into a bucket, never the sink
Read exit tickets and case files; draft strands 1 to 5 before Week 10

print_items: Worksheet x24 (2 sheets each, double-sided)
Evidence card pack x6 (1 A4 card sheet each, cut into 9 cards)
Evidence board x6 (A3 landscape)
Cleaning log card x6 (A5)
Statement frame x6 (A3); A4 alternative x24 (optional)
Self-assessment slip x24 (12 A4 sheets, cut in half)
Expert witness badges x6 (1 A4 sheet, cut out)

Concept cartoon x1 (A4 landscape) (optional)
Week 5 Ideas Parking Board photo print x1 (optional)
get_items: Blu Tack or glue sticks x6
Envelope x1
Camera or phone x1
reuse_items: Role cards and frame card sets x6
Week 8 results photos and board notes
hazards: No practical hazards beyond normal classroom rules.
Soil settling bottles stay sealed on the windowsill: look only, do not open.
watch_out: Keep cleaning log cards sealed in the envelope until Do minute 7, then give a full minute of quiet.
Never confirm the culprit, even if every group says Dr Huang; nobody reads a model conclusion aloud.
Y8_W09.language_note: Chinese welcome in talk; English key words in writing. Traps: contamination/contaminated, confidence/confident.
Y8_W09.next_week: Before Week 10: draft strands 1 to 5; return case files, frames. Print Week 10 set; optional prop to freezer.

Y8_W10.big_idea: Scientists defend conclusions with evidence, answer hard questions honestly (including what evidence does not show) and accept the result of checking.
goals: I can explain one piece of evidence: what we tested, how, what it shows and how sure we are.
I can answer or ask a question about evidence and reach a verdict on the strength of all of it.

flow.what: Same paper as Week 1, worked alone; 5-minute warning, collected at once; never shortened.
Teacher becomes judge; experts put on badges; juries take question cards and jury notes.
Six 90-second talks in evidence order, one jury question each; jury notes, feedback slip.
Exit ticket verdict (30 seconds), vote; teacher reads reveal card, 概要 lines; case closed.
Interest survey (3 minutes); thanks and certificates, or thanks if they come later.

Y8_W10.practical: No practical: groups give 90-second expert witness talks, answer a jury question; the class votes a verdict.
Y8_W10.assessment: Skills check (out of 20, vs Week 1); interest survey; strand 6 talk record; case files (strands 1 to 5); exit ticket.

prep_lines.text: Book Weeks 9 and 10 printing (once); agree certificate ceremony with lead
Book Week 1 reader or support for the skills check; make '15 seconds' card
Send print job (only designs rebuilt after the language pass)
Cut question cards (6 sets of 18), surveys, slips; staple checklists
Label slips by group; names in talk record; pick 概要 reader; check buddies
Optional: freeze an old notebook in a freezer bag overnight
Optional: print certificates for awards already fixed, if given today

prep_lines.when: On the day, before the lesson
prep_lines.text: Set out: papers face down, table packs, witness stand, timer, clipboard
Clean-up: skills checks first, surveys, case files; badges, cards in box
Sort feedback slips and reveal cards into group case files
Mark skills checks out of 20; enter tracker; finalise strands; check awards
Optional: enter question marks on the tracker's Question_analysis tab
Print and sign 25 certificates; skills reports; photos; programme summary
Optional: return Week 1 and 10 skills checks after marking and entry

Interest survey x24 (half A4, 2 per sheet, cut: 12 sheets)

Extra expert witness badge sheets x3 (6 per sheet, cut) (optional)
get_items: Timer visible to the class x1 (on-screen works)
Clipboard x1
Stapler and staples x1
'15 seconds' card x1 (hand-written)

Staff freezer space overnight (optional)

watch_out: Skills check as in Week 1: unaltered paper, same access, dictionaries away, never shortened.
Talk past 2 minutes: thank, move on. Short of time: 75-second talks, 3 questions; never skip verdict.
Y8_W10.language_note: Frames on the stand; 'My verdict is ___ because ___.' Band 1 sits by language buddy; Chinese answers count for Core.
Y8_W10.next_week: Last lesson. Then: mark, enter tracker, finalise strands, apply award rules; certificates within a week.
